caption: The post-training process described in Appendix <ref> decreases hallucinations. One measure is that the problems in SimpleQA—which the model very rarely gets correct—are increasingly not attempted during the course of post-training. We believe the final result is better behavior, even though the simple-evals score for SimpleQA (the F1 score) actually gives our base model a higher score than our final model.
model_annotation: This bar chart, titled "SimpleQA performance over the course of post-training," illustrates the distribution of model responses—categorized as Correct, Not Attempted, and Incorrect—for four stages: Base, SFT, DPO Stage 1, and Final, with the vertical axis labeled "Percentage (%)" ranging from 0 to 100 in linear increments. Each stage is represented by a stacked bar, with the bottom segment (green) indicating the percentage of Correct responses, the middle segment (dark blue) indicating Not Attempted, and the top segment (light blue) indicating Incorrect. For the Base stage, the values are 3.2% Correct, 6.8% Not Attempted, and 90.0% Incorrect. For SFT, the values are 3.7% Correct, 57.5% Not Attempted, and 38.7% Incorrect. For DPO Stage 1, the values are 2.9% Correct, 79.8% Not Attempted, and 17.4% Incorrect. For the Final stage, the values are 3.0% Correct, 81.1% Not Attempted, and 15.8% Incorrect. The bars are arranged horizontally from left to right in chronological order, and the segments are visually stacked with no sorting or emphasis applied to any particular bar.
